title: Leadership sync — rapid prep & action list (Mar 12 2026)
content:
Quick scratchpad for the 03/12 leadership sync — goal is to surface 3 decisions, 2 risks, and clear owners on follow-ups. Notes are intentionally terse; expand into slides only for items marked SLIDE.

Meeting objectives:
- Align on capacity and Dedicated renewals cadence for Q2 launch. SLIDE: capacity burn vs committed.
- Decide on conservative fallback policy for hosted API during region outages. (tradeoff: latency vs cost)
- Confirm timeline for Private GA (legal signoffs + on-prem packaging).

Key data to have on hand (callouts for Ravi/SRE):
- P50/P90 token latency last 7 days (hosted-v2) — highlight any regressions >10% week-over-week.
- Dedicated pool utilization: 72% across all pools; peak queue depth = 18 requests; tail latency spikes during 18:00-20:00 PT.
- Cost/revenue: Hosted API unit economics: $0.0009/token (avg) vs Dedicated committed discount 38%.

Talking points / scripts (short):
1) Capacity & Dedicated renewals — "We recommend a 10% headroom buffer in Q2 to avoid throttling for enterprise launches; tradeoffs and cost impact below." (Ravi to present numbers)
2) Fallback policy — "Opt for model-variant fallback by default; region-level reroute only for critical customers after approval." (Ops leads to confirm implementation risk)
3) Private GA timing — "Legal signoff expected by Mar 26; blockers: export control review + KMS integration test." (Elena to update)

Open questions to bring up (need answers pre-meeting):
- Can we implement per-customer circuit-breaker that scales with committed capacity by Apr 9? (SRE ask)
- Is quantization rollout for 7B models acceptable for Dedicated without quality regressions? (Research to confirm with evaluation harness)

Risks to call out (short):
- Risk A: Autoscaler misconfiguration leading to underprovision in EU region — mitigation: manual cap bump + canary policy for 48h.
- Risk B: Private packaging slip due to external vendor availability — mitigation: contingency plan to ship containerized image without vendor plugin.

Proposed decisions (ask for each):
- Approve 10% headroom on Dedicated pools for Q2 (Yes/No).
- Approve model-variant fallback as default graceful degradation policy (Yes/No).
- Confirm Private GA target date and go/no-go criteria (Target: Apr 30).

Follow-ups (owner / due / quick note) — convert to Jira tickets after meeting:
- AV-1: Prepare 1-slide capacity burn chart + 2 bullet conclusion (owner: Ravi Patel; due: 2026-03-11 EOD).
- AV-2: Draft fallback routing policy doc with sequence diagrams (owner: Kai Tan; due: 2026-03-18).
- AV-3: Run quantization evals on 7B set and produce fail/pass summary (owner: Sofia Morgan; due: 2026-03-16).
- AV-4: Legal to confirm export control checklist and signoff timeline (owner: Elena Rodriguez; due: 2026-03-24).
- AV-5: SRE to run simulated spike test in EU region and report queue depth safety margin (owner: Priya Singh; due: 2026-03-15).

Notes to self / meeting mechanics:
- Keep agenda to 40 minutes: 5m quick wins, 25m decisions, 10m follow-ups.
- Bring up the "canary fallback" demo only if someone asks for implementation detail (avoid derailing).
- If any decision is blocked, capture exact blocker and escalate to exec-ops sync same week.

Snackable TL;DR (two lines):
- We need a small capacity buffer + a default model-variant fallback to keep SLAs during Q2 growth.
- Key blockers: legal export control and quantization evals; tickets assigned and owners named above.
"Notes-to-self" rough TODOs post-meeting (private):
- Turn all AV- items into JIRA tickets before EOD + ping owners in Slack.
- Draft a single slide summarizing decisions for the all-hands if anything materially affects customers.
- Save a short summary email to exec-list with explicit asks and deadline dates.

End of scratchpad.
